name: Hà Nội
headline: City details, quiet corners, and evening light.

images.title: Low Sun Over West Lake
images.story: The autumn haze gave the setting sun a soft, pale orange circle with faint rays spilling up into the clouds. A clean stripe of gold stretched across the water toward the shore, ignoring the noisy ring of motorbikes behind me. It felt like the entire city paused for about ten minutes just to watch the heat drain out of the sky.

images.title: Skimming Past Turtle Tower
images.story: I was framing Tháp Rùa across the green, quiet water when a bird cut straight through the middle of the frame, low enough to throw its own faint shadow. The mossy arches looked heavy and centuries-old under the flat morning sky. It was one of those rare mornings where Hoàn Kiếm felt almost still.

images.title: Portrait by St. Joseph's
images.story: We took a walk down Nhà Thờ before the midday scooter rush could claim the entire asphalt. The weathered grey towers of the cathedral rose behind her, framed loosely by hanging banyan roots and the pale morning sky. She gave me that patient, familiar smile that said I had about two clicks before coffee called.

images.title: Regina Pacis Through the Gate
images.story: I rested the lens directly between the heavy iron gate bars to line up the Regina Pacis statue with the cathedral's gothic facade. A fresh bowl of white orchids sat quietly at the base of the pedestal, catching the midday heat. The darkened stone and the vertical crop gave the courtyard an unexpectedly quiet weight in the middle of the city.

images.title: Posing by the Painted Shutter
images.story: She had set up her tripod stick right against a painted rolling shutter, completely owning the sidewalk while the street traffic buzzed past. Her oversized sunglasses and ruffled tunic gave the whole scene an effortless runway vibe against the weathered metal slats. I caught her between takes, perfectly composed while checking her screen.

images.title: Ceramic Thinker and His Dog
images.story: Among the rows of glazed turtles and painted deities, this shirtless terracotta figure had the most wonderfully resigned expression, resting his chin on his knees. Right beside him, a little dog with a yellow collar stared up as if waiting for permission to bark. It captured that dry, gentle street humor you stumble upon only when you stop rushing through the Old Quarter.

images.title: Bougainvillea Arching the Canal
images.story: A thick tangle of magenta bougainvillea spills across the canal railings, nearly swallowing the concrete bridges whole. Behind the pink blossoms, identical apartment towers loom tall against a pale late-afternoon sky. It feels like the city's wilder greenery quietly reclaiming whatever corner it can find.
